item.title: Chip Kelly's old-school gamble, Northwestern's new-school vision have Wildcats dreaming of the College Football Playoff
item.description: EVANSTON, Ill. — Against the window seal of David Braun’s office conference room at Northwestern , a bronze statue of a man glares toward visitors. An award Braun won in 2023, the miniature depiction of Bear Bryant, dressed in his trademark suit and a houndstooth hat, is fitting considering the program’s upward trajectory and that his offense, under new coordinator Chip Kelly, is showing flashes of yesteryear: the Wing-T, Wishbone and option concepts that Bryant used to claim six national championships at Alabama more than four decades ago. “You can call them dated. That’s not fair,” Braun says with a smile. “But creative!” Life is good here in this northern Chicago suburb. The 6-1 and 18th-ranked Wildcats are off to their best start since 2012; the fall foliage sweeps across this campus like a painter’s brush; the university alignment and athletic investment is as its best since before the tumult around the clumsy handling of the end of the Pat Fitzgerald era; the program opened a more than $850 million new stadium earlier this season; and the offense is an entertaining throwback under one of the sport’s most heralded gurus. On an unseasonably warm Thursday from the school’s shimmering football facility, Kelly gnashes on breadsticks as a laminated sheet of offensive schemes protrudes from his backpocket. Two days from now he returns to Eugene for Northwestern’s game against a reeling Oregon team. He audibly shrugs. He’s returned to Oregon before, both as UCLA’s head coach and as Ohio State’s offensive coordinator in 2024. In fact, Kelly is 0-4 against the Ducks. “They’re a really good football team. They’re really talented,” he said. “Turn the tape on and you stop thinking about being nostalgic.” In his first season back in college after an 11-game stint coordinating the Raiders offense, Kelly has infused some of his old tricks into the Wildcats. He’s embracing formations, schemes and concepts that he says he hasn’t used since his days as offensive coordinator at New Hampshire — more than 20 years ago. Northwestern QB Aidan Chiles walks off the field with Chip Kelly following a win over Michigan State. (Adam Ruff/Getty Images) Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Upon an evaluation of the Northwestern roster during the offseason, Kelly arrived at a decision based on the talent before him: It’s time to take it old school. He had a 6-foot-4, 225-pound quarterback with wide receiver speed (Michigan State transfer Aiden Chiles) and a bevy of running backs in what is the team’s deepest position. He dusted off his proverbial binders from his days at FCS New Hampshire: the Wing-T formation, Wishbone schemes and military academy option plays. Braun, a former defensive coordinator who hired Kelly in December, recalls watching Northwestern’s offense practice this offseason and, at times, thinking, “What are we doing?” And then the games got going and, well, kaboom. item.description: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Will Wade lands 5-star guard, son of former NBA PG in major LSU recruiting win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LSU basketball and coach Will Wade compensated for the loss of RJ Luis immediately . The Tigers instead pulled off a massive College Basketball Recruiting win Thursday. This one involving five-star point guard Reese Alston, the son of NBA star Rafer. And Alston turned down two SEC rivals of the Tigers in making his decision. “Alston chose the Tigers over Louisville, although he also took official visits to Kentucky, Tennessee and Wichita State, all of which were on his final list of schools,” the reporters wrote. He brings his own smooth craftiness on the floor just like his famed dad, who rose to fame as street ball legend “Skip 2 My Lou.” The elder Alston starred at Fresno State under the late Jerry Tarkanian before scoring 6,799 career points in the NBA. item.title: ‘Not a tension-free zone’: Joe Buck and Troy Aikman reportedly still not happy
item.description: ESPN/ABC Monday Night Football commentators Joe Buck, left, and Troy Aikman before the Detroit Lions vs. Las Vegas Raiders game at Ford Field, Monday, Oct. 30, 2023. Joe Buck and Troy Aikman have called NFL games together for 25 seasons, and on the air, they still sound like the same old partners. But behind the scenes, things reportedly haven’t gotten much better between them. According to a new report, the friction between ESPN’s Monday Night Football duo hasn’t gone away, even after conversations with network leadership. One source said the situation is “not a tension-free zone,” and Aikman is reportedly almost certain to land somewhere else next season. Buck and Aikman’s Blowup The tension stems from the two broadcasters’ very different contract situations. Buck signed a six-year extension worth roughly $108 million that The Athletic revealed in September. Aikman, meanwhile, is in the final season of the five-year, $90 million deal he signed when the pair left Fox for ESPN in 2022. Front Office Sports’ Ryan Glasspiegel first reported the rift , revealing that Buck confronted Aikman about the friction before the Bills’ overtime win over the Rams on Oct. 12. Puck’s Dylan Byers later reported more details . According to Byers, Aikman had grown cold and curt with Buck for weeks before the confrontation and accused his partner of betraying him, since Buck’s extension had reportedly been finalized months earlier without Aikman being told. Buck later apologized to the production crew for his role in the blowup. ‘Not a Tension-Free Zone’ While Buck and Aikman have been able to keep things professional on the air, Byers reports in his latest newsletter that the friction persists, though ongoing dialogue with ESPN leadership has slightly eased the strain. “It’s not a tension-free zone,” one source told Byers, via Awful Announcing . That wasn’t obvious during Monday’s Eagles-Cowboys broadcast, which Byers called “another drama-free broadcast.” Buck got a laugh out of Aikman with a joke about Michael Irvin’s sideline celebrations, and the two did a cordial postgame hit on SportsCenter , according to The Philadelphia Inquirer . Byers credited both broadcasters’ professionalism for keeping their issues off the air. But according to his reporting, Aikman appears almost certain to be somewhere else next season. Clearly, if this is the end of the line for one of the NFL’s longest-running booths, both men are determined to finish it out without letting fans see the cracks. The post ‘Not a tension-free zone’: Joe Buck and Troy Aikman reportedly still not happy appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: What needs to happen for Bengals to beat Tennessee, improve to 5-2
item.description: If you're doing a side by side comparison of the Cincinnati Bengals and Tennessee Titans , it'd be easy to assume the Nov. 1 meeting at Paycor Stadium would be a one-sided contest just based on their records. Cincinnati looks like an ascending, 4-2 team while the Titans are 1-6, and made a trade Oct. 29 that looks intended to jumpstart a rebuild effort. Jason Williams Ring of Honor Trumpy How Bengals compare to Chiefs, Steelers in honoring legends | Williams The fact is that the Titans have been as much of a handful as a 1-6 team can be. Four of their six losses were one-possession games ( Eagles , Giants , Ravens , Browns ) with an average margin of defeat in those contests of 4.5 points. Their lone win came against the 2-4 Indianapolis Colts . If could be exactly the kind of game where the Bengals get stuck in a nail-biter, especially considering Cincinnati is still yet to play a complete game in which the team impressed in every phase. As the calendar flips from October to November, and the Bengals enter the meat of their 2026 schedule, here's what needs to happen in order for Cincinnati to improve to 5-2 ahead of a key stretch of games: Show Cincinnati, Bengals fans, observers your true identity This is less an objective to accomplish in-game and more a plea from fans and media types seeking to pinpoint what kind of Bengals team we're looking at in 2026. Because entering Week 8, it seems fair to say many people have difficulty trying to pinpoint what we're looking at. Even the signature win - the Week 7 victory that was an embarrassment-turned-mauling against the Ravens - was, as Bengals head coach Zac Taylor conceded, a good half of football as opposed to a complete game, which it certainly wasn't. The Bengals have been carried by their defense at times (Weeks 1-3 versus Tampa Bay, Houston and Jacksonville), and eventually carried by the offense against the Ravens. The closest we've seen the team to playing complete, balanced football might have been the loss to Pittsburgh (putting aside that day's special teams major malfunctions). Bottom line, it's now Week 8. The Bengals are on the precipice of a stretch of games (at Madrid versus Atlanta followed by back-to-back primetime games on U.S. soil against Pittsburgh and Washington) that will more than likely dictate if its a legitimate contender for the AFC North title, or if it's destined for the mad scramble for a Wild Card berth. It's time for this team to grow into what it is supposed to be. That doesn't mean it has to reach its peak form. In fact, you'd prefer that happens closer to playoff time, but a baseline of higher-level performance from each unit should be expected. Put a full game together against the Titans. Handle your business convincingly, and show us who you are. There's no excuse for Joe Burrow to face sustained pressured from Titans. item.title: One glaring matchup problem Georgia can’t hide against Florida
item.description: One of the great college football rivalry games kicks off during Saturday’s Week 9 action. And while one side of this matchup is a big favorite, the underdog could have one advantage on the field that can make this close. As No. 3 Georgia prepares to face No. 17 Florida on Saturday, one matchup deserves particular attention: the Gators’ rushing attack against a Bulldogs defense that has recently shown signs of vulnerability on the ground. More: Predicting SEC football scores for Week 9 games Can the Gators run on the Bulldogs? Sep 12, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; Florida Gators running back Jadan Baugh (13) rushes with the ball against the Campbell Fighting Camels during the first half at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Georgia enters the game allowing just 91.4 rushing yards per game, ranking as the nation’s No. 10 run defense. But over its last two appearances, this unit has not played up to its standard when going against opposing running backs. Georgia allowed 161 rushing yards in its three-point win at Alabama and then surrendered another 192 on the ground in its upset loss to unranked Auburn the week after. Those performances suggest that sustained ground production can challenge Georgia’s defensive structure, even if it doesn’t exactly guarantee a victory. Florida has the firepower to test Georgia Florida has a potential difference-maker in running back Jadan Baugh. The SEC’s third-most productive back has amassed 763 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns and is a proven option capable of controlling possession and creating chances in the red zone. Florida averages 194.3 rushing yards per game, fourth in the SEC, putting its ground attack in position to test Georgia’s defensive discipline. Moreover, Jon Sumrall-coached teams are an elite 37-3 in their last 40 games when they finish with at least 125 rushing yards. That should be the Gators’ secret weapon to shorten the game against a Bulldog front that allows under 3 yards per carry. How Georgia can counter Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) passes under pressure from Florida Gators linebacker Myles Graham (5) during the first half of an NCAA football game at Everbank Stadium in Jacksonville, FL on Saturday, November 1, 2025. [Alan Youngblood/Gainesville Sun] Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Despite recent success, the Gators have reason for caution. Baugh was held to just 13 rushing yards against Missouri and only 59 against South Carolina. Both were ugly losses for Florida. Ultimately, the Gators’ clearest path to making this rivalry competitive is to establish Baugh early and sustain their ground attack. If they can replicate the rushing pressure Auburn created, Georgia could face its most consequential defensive test of the season. item.title: Trio of Beaver Valley runners win gold at WPIAL cross-country championships
item.description: WHITE OAK — It was a historic day for Beaver Valley high school cross country runners for a variety of ways, with individuals capturing multiple WPIAL titles, a freshman capturing her first WPIAL title, and a team putting up an unprecedented finish at the 2026 WPIAL cross country championships at White Oak Park on Thursday, Oct. 29. Two of the top boys distance runners in the state, Quaker Valley’s Jonah Montagnese and Sewickley Academy’s Zach Sharara, had gold on their minds after winning the Class 2A and 1A crowns in 2025. The pair joined rare history in the Beaver Valley, with Montagnese and Sharara becoming the sixth and seventh runners in the area’s history to win two straight WPIAL championships. “I feel super lucky to be able to come back here and blessed to win again,” Montagnese said. “It is a great achievement to have and one that I always want to have and add to the resume.” The Virginia commit finished 23 seconds ahead of the silver medalist, North Catholic’s Jack Steineman, but knew it wasn’t his best race, finishing four seconds behind the time that won him the 2A title last season. With thoughts of doubt swirling in Montagnese’s mind and Steineman trying to make a push at the defending champ, the senior pushed through. “When we hit the two-mile mark, there was a lot of doubt in my mind about this race,” Montagnese said. “I tried to work through some of the pain, take a deep breath and close hard. I was glad I was able to do that. Sharara continued his dominant run against 1A competition at this year’s championships, finishing with a time of 15:49.3. “It feels really good to go back-to-back here at WPIALs,” Sharara said. “I have been working really hard and improved a lot during the summer. Coming into the race, I didn’t care about the time that I ran; I just wanted to sit at the front, control the pace and kick it in on the final stretch.” For the beginning stages of the race, Sharara and Winchester Thurston’s Jack Iyer sat almost stride-for-stride with each other. But towards the latter half of the race, Sharara found another gear and finished just over six seconds in front to claim his second gold. “I think that I waited a little too long to push because it kind of got close towards the end,” Sharara said. “But I still think that I executed the race well was able to build a lead.” Now, after capturing another WPIAL title, Sharara has his sights set at the PIAA championships after winning bronze in Hershey last season . While the race will be at a new course at Big Springs High School, the Sewickley Academy junior is ready for the challenge of a new course. “I wasn’t really a big fan of the Hershey course, so I am very excited to run at this course at states,” Sharara said. “It’s a new challenge; I enjoy it, the course runs fast and I am excited to compete with some of the fastest runners in the state.” Riverside freshman standout PR’s en route to Class 2A title Riverside’s Reese Anderson has put together a freshman year to rememb

item.title: Red Sox Trade Nate Eaton to A’s: Details and What This Means
item.description: Sep 30, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; Boston Red Sox outfielder Nate Eaton (18) hits a double in the third inning against the New York Yankees during game two of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Cre… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor The Boston Red Sox have traded outfielder Nate Eaton to the Athletics for right-handed prospect Jareth Rayo , per Bob Nightengale and Chris Cotillo. Eaton was a valuable depth piece for the Red Sox, as he provided a spot for a pinch runner late in games, as well as a stellar fielder in limited appearances. Red Sox get 18-year-old right-handed pitcher Jareth Rayo from A’s for Nate Eaton, confirmed. https://t.co/PwXomVPXFj — Chris Cotillo (@ChrisCotillo) October 29, 2026 Nate Eaton Traded: Details Eaton’s Red Sox Career: What the Athletics Get Eaton has been a decent player who’s come up in some huge moments for the Red Sox. In 2025, he was seen as a platoon guy, mainly killing it against right-handers , as he hit .316 against them that season. Overall, he hit .296 in 2025. While he did fall off in average in 2026, batting .160 in fewer games, he did bat well in the limited appearances with runners in scoring position. He hit three for eight in those opportunities (a batting average of .375), which was remarkably higher than 2025, where he hit .143 in that situation. Sep 20, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Boston Red Sox outfielder Nate Eaton (18) catches a fly ball during the second inning against Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images Fielding-wise, he’s also above average. Other than a failed experiment at third base (-3 DRS in 73 innings), he has been pretty solid throughout his Red Sox tenure, especially this season in the outfield. With the acquisition of Jahmai Jones , and finding playing time for Jarren Duran , Eli White , and Roman Anthony post-injury, it was extremely hard to find playing time for all seven of these outfielders (including gold glovers Ceddanne Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu ). In some capacity, though, it all worked out. And Eaton had an underrated glove, with a DRS of five in the outfield for 2026. Eaton will be a solid depth piece for the Athletics next season. Who is Jareth Rayo? As for the Red Sox’s return on this deal, they received minor leaguer Rayo, an 18-year-old pitcher from Nicaragua. He made his professional debut in the Dominican Summer League with the Athletics this season, and didn’t have the greatest success. In nine starts, he went 1-1 with an ERA of 5.50. This also includes 8.5 hits per nine innings and 1.3 homers per nine innings. As he is an international signee and in the DSL, Rayo seems like a complete gamble, but time will tell if he works out in the future. There’s plenty of time to track how he does. Why Do This Trade? item.title: Max Verstappen discusses toll of F1 calendar after two drivers fall ill
item.description: Motorsport photo Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen says it is "normal" for F1 drivers and team members to fall ill at this stage of the season after two drivers missed Thursday's media day in Mexico City. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was excused from media duties while he recovers from a viral illness, with Mercedes expecting the Italian driver to return to the track for Friday practice. Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas also missed media day through illness, with the American outfit describing it as a precaution. Mexico is the second race of a triple-header after the United States Grand Prix last week and ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix next week. The last nine race weekends of the 2026 season are arranged into three triple-headers with one-week breaks in between them. While speaking to the media in Mexico, Verstappen was asked how tough the run of races had been. "It is, of course, always quite tough on your body, like three weeks in a row. Sometimes you can get a little bit unlucky with whatever, a stomach bug," the Dutchman explained. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, congratulates pole man Daniel Ricciardo, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, congratulates pole man Daniel Ricciardo, Red Bull Racing "But it's normally around this time of the year that not only drivers, but mechanics and people in the team get sick. Because your body can take a lot of stress. But at one point, of course, it also tells you when it needs a little recovery phase. "That's something that you need to stay on top of. And some years it goes a bit better than others. I think you try to learn about it as well a little bit with the more seasons that you do. Sometimes some things are things that you can't prevent. But for sure, it's always very tough. "For me, the toughest bit is that you can't really go home in between to be back with the family. That, for me, is nowadays something that I do not really enjoy about triple-headers." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Vanoli frustrated by Fiorentina defending: ‘Team has talent, but must work together’
item.description: Vanoli frustrated by Fiorentina defending: ‘Team has talent, but must work together’ Paolo Vanoli was frustrated by Fiorentina’s defending after a 2-2 draw with Atalanta . ‘This is a talented squad, but we need to defend together.’ The Viola were in crisis after three consecutive defeats, so risked crumbling after going into the break 1-0 down to a Charles De Ketelaere goal when they otherwise had a strong first half performance. They came out fighting and turned it around through the Alieu Njie diving header and deflected Joao Mario effort, but Nicola Zalewski sealed the 2-2 result. Vanoli frustrated by Fiorentina FLORENCE, ITALY – OCTOBER 29: Head coach Paolo Vanoli manager of ACF Fiorentina and Alex Jimenez Sanchez known as Alex of ACF Fiorentina reacts during the Serie A match between ACF Fiorentina and Atalanta BC at Stadio Artemio Franchi on October 29, 2026 in Florence, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) “The regret is that we didn’t win a game after playing very well,” Vanoli told DAZN Italia. “We have these blackouts that are proving very costly and we cannot keep conceding goals in this manner. Fortunately, we got back into the match, but we’ve got to be more determined mentally when defending.” There were a few surprises in the starting XI this evening, above all Joao Mario as a full-back, but it paid off with a goal. FLORENCE, ITALY – OCTOBER 29: Joao Mario of ACF Fiorentina in action during the Serie A match between ACF Fiorentina and Atalanta BC at Stadio Artemio Franchi on October 29, 2026 in Florence, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) “We are a team that plays well, but must learn how to defend, that is what we are lacking,” noted Vanoli. “Those two goals were really gifted to Atalanta. Every match is like a puzzle, we have a lot to work on. This is a talented squad, that is not in doubt, but Italian football requires you to all defend together as a unit. “On the first goal, Cher Ndour didn’t follow De Ketelaere, while on the second we were all sluggish. We lack street smarts, such as in the game with Inter where we threw it away.” FLORENCE, ITALY – OCTOBER 29: David de Gea goalkeeper of ACF Fiorentina reacts after against goal of Torino FC Charles De Ketelaere of Atalanta BC during the Serie A match between ACF Fiorentina and Atalanta BC at Stadio Artemio Franchi on October 29, 2026 in Florence, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) Fiorentina could’ve been traumatised by that defeat at San Siro, a game they were winning 1-0 only to lose 2-1 with two goals conceded in added time. Vanoli was asked if taking Niccolò Fagioli off at half-time was a tactical decision and he confirmed that it was not down to fitness issues. Fiorentina, Udinese and Parma are all locked together on five points , with only Venezia behind them at rock bottom on three.

item.title: Where Is Sidney Crosby on NHL's All-Time Points List? Penguins Star Keeps Moving Up Leaderboard
item.description: Where Is Sidney Crosby on NHL's All-Time Points List? Penguins Star Keeps Moving Up Leaderboard originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Sidney Crosby continues to climb the NHL's all-time scoring leaderboard, with another major milestone within reach as the Pittsburgh Penguins captain prepares for Thursday night's game. Crosby enters the matchup with 1,768 career points, putting him seventh in NHL history. He is just three points shy of tying Marcel Dionne for sixth place, with an opportunity to move closer to another spot among the league's all-time greats. Dionne finished his NHL career with 1,771 points across 1,348 games. Crosby has reached 1,768 points while continuing his 22nd NHL season, adding to a career that has kept him among the league's most productive players for more than two decades. Crosby would tie Dionne with three points and move into sole possession of sixth place with his fourth point. NHL All-Time Points Leaders The NHL's all-time scoring leaderboard features some of the most recognizable names in hockey history. Wayne Gretzky remains comfortably atop the list with 2,857 career points. Here is where the top 10 currently stand: Wayne Gretzky — 2,857 points Jaromir Jagr — 1,921 points Mark Messier — 1,887 points Gordie Howe — 1,850 points Ron Francis — 1,798 points Marcel Dionne — 1,771 points Sidney Crosby — 1,768 points Steve Yzerman — 1,755 points Mario Lemieux — 1,723 points Alex Ovechkin — 1,691 points Crosby has already passed several legendary players on the leaderboard, including former Penguins teammate Mario Lemieux, who finished his career with 1,723 points. The next target is Dionne, but the climb does not stop there. Ron Francis holds fifth place with 1,798 points, leaving Crosby 30 points away from reaching that mark. item.title: Osimhen welcomes second child with Cameroonian-German girlfriend
item.description: Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen and his girlfriend, Stefanie Ladewig, have welcomed their second child, a baby girl named Liora Audrey. Galatasaray, the Turkish club where Osimhen plays, announced the arrival of the couple’s daughter in a social media post on Thursday. “Our Football A Team player Victor Osimhen and Stefanie have welcomed a baby girl into the world. “We congratulate the couple Victor and Stefanie; we wish their newborn baby Liora Audrey a long, healthy, and happy life!” the post read. The couple’s first daughter, Hailey, was born in October 2022. Ladewig, a Cameroonian-German fashion model and social media influencer, reportedly began dating Osimhen in 2019 when the Nigerian forward was playing for German Bundesliga side Wolfsburg. Earlier this month, reports emerged that Ladewig had been involved in a road accident while heavily pregnant. Turkish media reported that she escaped unhurt in the crash, which involved three vehicles. Meanwhile, Osimhen is expected to feature for Galatasaray in their league fixture against T. Konyaspor on Friday, having been included in the squad for the match. The 27-year-old forward was in impressive form on Monday, scoring twice to help Galatasaray defeat their fierce Istanbul rivals, Fenerbahce, in the city derby. Galatasaray currently lead the league standings after nine matches, while Osimhen has scored eight goals, placing him among the competition’s joint-top scorers. The post Osimhen welcomes second child with Cameroonian-German girlfriend appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Patriots’ AJ Brown doesn’t practice but gets encouraging update from coach
item.description: Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Patriots’ AJ Brown doesn’t practice but gets encouraging update from coach appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots are hoping to have A.J. Brown in the lineup Sunday when they face the Miami Dolphins in South Florida, but he did not take part in Thursday’s practice with what the team called knee and ankle issues. AJ Brown (knee/ankle) did not participate in practice today. https://t.co/hat1YJ6dvq — Phil Perry (@PhilAPerry) October 29, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It seems a bit discouraging because Brown was a limited participant in Wednesday’s practice session, but did not get on the field to work out with his teammates a day later. However, Patriots wide receivers coach Todd Downing did not seem concerned or alarmed about the development. “I’m not worried about where A.J.’s at, at all,” Downing said , per MassLive Patriots reporter Mark Daniels. Brown has had multiple injury issues in his first season with the Patriots. The former Philadelphia Eagles star suffered an ankle injury in the season opener against the Seattle Seahawks. He has been in the lineup for the last two games and he has contributed 6 receptions for 75 yards. He has not looked like a dangerous, big-play performer to this point, and that’s just what the Patriots are hoping he becomes the rest of the season. At this point, the Patriots have been depending on tight end Hunter Henry and wideouts Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas as quarterback Drake Maye ’s primary receivers. Henry has been targeted 31 times, and he has 26 receptions for 296 yards and 2 TDs. Doubs has caught 14 passes for 261 yards for 3 touchdowns and he looks like he is starting to get used to playing in the Patriots system after coming over from the Green Bay Packers. Douglas has added 23-256-3 and he clearly has an important role in the Patriots’ offensive game plan. item.title: Max Verstappen jokes about Daniel Ricciardo's Le Mans ambition: "He's a smart man picking me!"
item.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen has joked that former Red Bull team-mate Daniel Ricciardo is a "smart man" for picking him in a potential trio for a future Le Mans 24 Hour challenge. Ricciardo has not taken part in any racing series since leaving F1 for the second time having raced for Red Bull's sister RB squad in 2024. However, speaking on the Beyond the Grid podcast, the Australian race winner suggested that he would be tempted to take part in a future edition of the 24-hour race around La Circuit de la Sarthe in France, highlighting Verstappen and another former Red Bull team-mate in Sebastian Vettel as a dream line-up. “I don’t want to put pressure on him, but obviously Max is a name that would be high on the list," replied Ricciardo when asked who he would choose for a partnership. Read Also: Why Daniel Ricciardo would consider a comeback at Le Mans "We talked about Red Bull obviously in 2018, and what if, and what if; I was trying to get back at the team at the end of my career, so maybe that’s a way that we could give the people what they want." Verstappen has previously mentioned a desire to one day compete at Le Mans and has dovetailed his F1 priorities with outings in GT racing, taking part in this year's Nurburgring 24 Hours and the GT World Challenge finale at Portimao. Asked ahead of this weekend's Mexico City GP about Ricciardo's comments, Verstappen replied: "He's a smart man to choose me in the car. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing "But we have to see. It just depends on a lot of things. Also for me, if I want to do it, I want to do it properly with really good prep. "At the moment I cannot do that. I don't have the free time to dedicate to a Le Mans project with all the other things that I'm also doing outside of Formula 1." Ricciardo's suggestion that Le Mans could be on the table is the first time he has revealed a desire to get back into a race car publicly, though Verstappen revealed that the news was "not new to me" having conversed with Ricciardo. "Yeah, we have spoken," confirmed the four-time world champion. "But also, I think either from my side or his side, I don't think we are the types that always need to share everything. We talk about a lot of things in the background. "I think he said it himself. He doesn't see himself coming back for a whole season but the one-offs can interest him. Why not? But again, I think if we do something like that, he will for sure agree that it needs to be proper. It needs to be for a chance to win. "For a chance to win against people that do it a whole season, you need to be prepared really well. You just need to find the right timing." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Chancellor Lee Adams prepares for Special Olympics equestrian competition
item.description: Chancellor Lee Adams has joined a team of 12 athletes from Victory Farm in Gastonia to train for the Special Olympics equestrian competition. The team traveled to the Tryon International Equestrian Center in Mill Spring, North Carolina, to compete in the Southeast Regional Equestrian Tournament. Adams lives with cerebral palsy and has ridden horses on and off for years as physical therapy. The training has strengthened his core and legs, enabling him to take steps without relying on his walker. Victory Farm Head Instructor Dory Pell emphasized that the event is a rigorous athletic competition rather than a passive exercise. “So many people assume that we put these riders on a horse and we lead them through a course or we lead them around the ring. It is no pony ride! It is a true competition where they have to learn skills and ability. They are going to work through challenges such as making their body do what they didn’t think it was capable of,” Pell said. ALSO READ: Chancellor Lee Adams turns 26 Chancellor Lee Adams competes in two separate divisions: showmanship and working trail. In showmanship, Adams must lead his horse, Dore-Ry, through a memorized course. The working trail division simulates riding through the woods. “And that is one that has a lot of different obstacles and patterns. He has to remember all the patterns and obstacles and execute them to perfection. In the proper order,” Pell said. During practice, Adams worked on navigating obstacles, including stopping on a raised wooden platform and commanding his horse, “Whoa! 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.” Pell praised his commitment during training sessions. “That young man is so devoted to getting this done that he just works and works and works. He never wants to stop. We’re the ones that have to stop him because he wants to make sure he gets it right,” Pell said, describing his effort as “It’s astounding.” Adams was born after a November 1999 attack orchestrated by his father, former Carolina Panthers player Rae Carruth. Carruth hired a gunman who shot Adams’ mother, Cherica Adams, while she was pregnant. Cherica Adams died from her injuries, but Chancellor Lee Adams survived the shooting. ALSO READ: Rae Carruth sends son money after being released from prison Saundra Adams, the grandmother who has raised Adams since birth, said participating in the competition gives him valuable encouragement. “The extra ata’ boy, he’s doing good. You know, he needs that encouragement. You know, and I think that’s good for all children, not just children with special needs, all children and adults. We need to hear that. You know, you really did good. And this is, you know, this is not something that’s just giving him an award. He’s earning it!” Saundra Adams said. In addition to physical training, Saundra Adams focused on preparing her grandson emotionally for the competition. “We’ve talked about that at home, and he understands that, you know, not everybody may get first place. Not everybody’s gonna get first

item.title: Max Verstappen responds to Daniel Ricciardo’s Le Mans dream team call
item.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen has joked that his former team-mate Daniel Ricciardo is "a smart man" for picking him for his dream Le Mans line-up. In fact, he revealed that the pair of them had already discussed the possibility of it. In a recent interview with the Beyond the Grid podcast, the Australian talked about his time at Red Bull and his exit from Formula 1. While he discussed what was next for him, he said that a Le Mans entry could be on the list. When asked who he'd team up with, Max Verstappen was the first name on his list. Sebastian Vettel was also an option, making something he called a "nice little Red Bull reunion" of sorts. “He’s a smart man to choose me in the car," Verstappen joked. "But we have to see. It just depends on a lot of things.” The four-time world champion has made no secret of his interest in endurance racing with him recently competing at Portimao, where he and his team finished ninth. He did, however, stress that he would only take on Le Mans with full preparation. “Also for me, if I want to do it, I want to do it proper with really good prep. And at the moment I cannot do that. I don’t have the time - the free time to dedicate to a Le Mans project with all the other things that I’m also doing outside of Formula 1.” Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, congratulates pole man Daniel Ricciardo, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, congratulates pole man Daniel Ricciardo, Red Bull Racing Ricciardo’s comments were the first time he had publicly spoken about racing again in any real capacity. But Verstappen said the idea had already come up between them. “This is not new to me, of course. Yeah, we have spoken,” he said. “I don’t think we are the types that always need to share everything. We talk about a lot of things in the background.” Ricciardo said a full season of racing did not appeal, and Verstappen believes that a one-off would only be worthwhile if they could be seriously competitive. “He doesn’t see himself coming back for a whole race, like a season. But the one-offs can interest him. Why not? “But again, I think if we do something like that, he will for sure agree that it needs to be proper. It needs to be for a chance to win. For a chance to win against people that do it a whole season, you need to be prepared really well. You just need to find the right timings.” Verstappen and Ricciardo were team-mates at Red Bull from 2016 to 2018. Ricciardo said on the podcast that a shared Le Mans entry could be a way to “give the people what they want” after the pair’s split at the end of 2018. Why Daniel Ricciardo would consider a comeback at Le Mans Daniel Ricciardo opens door to racing return with Max Verstappen at Le Mans To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Willock Gets 7.5, Dedic With 5.5 | Newcastle United Players Rated In Poor Loss Vs Everton
item.description: Willock Gets 7.5, Dedic With 5.5 | Newcastle United Players Rated In Poor Loss Vs Everton Newcastle United faced off against Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium earlier tonight as they hoped to secure a good result on the road in the EFL Cup. The Magpies made a slow start to the game and conceded the opening goal in the 34th minute when James Garner found the back of the net. Hayden Hackney doubled the home side’s advantage in the 45th minute as Newcastle went into the half-time break 2-0 down on the scoreline. Thierno Barry made it 3-0 to Everton in the 69th minute. However, Dan Burn got a goal back for the Tyneside club in the 88th minute. The match ended with Matthias Jaissle’s men suffering a poor 3-1 loss away from home. Let’s take a look at how each Newcastle United player fared during the clash against the Toffees. He made a couple of solid saves at the back, but failed to keep things solid at the back. RB: Amar Dedic – 5.5/10 Dedic did his fair share of defending but made a costly error tonight. CB: Fabian Schar – 6/10 He cleared his lines when he could and was a threat at the other end of the field. CB: Dan Burn – 7/10 Burn put his foot through the ball when needed and managed to score late in the game. LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 29: William Osula of Newcastle United shoots under pressure from James Tarkowski of Everton during the Carabao Cup Fourth Round match between Everton and Newcastle United at Hill Dickinson Stadium on October 29, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Jan Kruger/Getty Images) LB: Lewis Hall – 7/10 He was a positive influence at both ends of the field. CM: Nico Gonzalez – 6/10 Gonzalez earned possession back once and made a few decent chances in the final third. CM: Jacob Ramsey – 6/10 He worked hard defensively but offered very little going forward. RW: Jacob Murphy – 6/10 Murphy was not shy of having a strike at goal and was replaced in the 66th minute. CAM: Joe Willock – 7.5/10 He engineered a lot of inviting chances for his teammates to score and has an assist to show for his efforts. LW: Harvey Barnes – 6.5/10 Barnes managed to shine at times in the first half, but there was no goal for him. ST: William Osula – 6/10 He struggled to be a threat up top and was replaced at half-time. CM: Joelinton – 6.5/10 He was good on the ball. ST: Yoane Wissa – 6.5/10 Wissa was lively after coming off the bench. RW: Anthony Elanga – 6/10 He made one key chance in the final third. LW: Bazoumana Traore – 6.5/10 He made two decent runs with the ball.

item.title: Two Reasons Brewers Will Be Even Better Next Season
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers shortstop Jesus Made The Milwaukee Brewers won the World Series, but it may be just the beginning of a long run. Last season, the Brewers won the most games in baseball but failed to reach the World Series. This year, they also won the most games in baseball, but got the job done. The signs were there last year, but this season they were undeniable. The scary part is that they did it with some clear flaws and are going to be even better next season. Starting Rotation Will Be Much Better In 2027 For much of the year, Jacob Misiorowski, Logan Henderson and Kyle Harrison looked to be a trio that was going to carry the Brewers through October. However, Harrison had a very rough second half, losing his spot in the rotation. He did not look the same after his forearm injury, but before that, he had a 2.57 ERA through his first 15 starts. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Harrison hit a bump, but the team is expecting him to come back looking like the player he was early in the year. The Brewers went through the postseason without even using him, and having him back in the rotation will be huge if he is pitching as he did in the first half. Knowing the Brewers' track record with pitching, there's little reason to believe he won't be back to form. Then there's Robert Gasser, who spent the first half of the year struggling. However, he ended the regular season on a roll and was phenomenal in the postseason. He made three starts, all on the road, and pitched great in all of them. He will be going into next season as one of the best starters on the team. Finally, the arm everyone has forgotten about: Quinn Priester. In 2025, he made 29 appearances for the Brewers. He made 24 starts and was a bulk pitcher or pitched behind an opener in the other outings. He had a 3.32 ERA in 2025, and was one of the best starters on the team. He missed this season with injury, but is on track to be ready for spring training. A rotation of Misiorowski, Henderson, Gasser, Harrison and Priester going into next year is much better than what they had this year overall. They also have Brandon Sproat, Shane Drohan and Coleman Crow as options to start. Top Prospect In Baseball Is Coming If fans thought Jackson Chourio was good, they're going to be shocked to learn the Brewers have another teenager in the minor leagues knocking on the door. Jesús Made is the No. 1 prospect in baseball and could be on the team as soon as opening day. Like Chourio, many expect the Brewers to sign him to an extension, and at some point next season, he will be in Milwaukee. He is a shortstop, but the Brewers have a history of taking shortstops and moving them to second base or third base. Look at Brice Turang or Caleb Durbin last year, for example. Made could move to third base, and there's an argument to be made that he would instantly be better than the platoon of Joey Ortiz and David Hamilton. Third base

item.title: ‘We Got Our Swagger Back’ – Angel Reese Makes Feelings Clear After Dream Force Game 7 in WNBA Finals
item.description: 'We Got Our Swagger Back' - Angel Reese Makes Feelings Clear After Dream Force Game 7 in WNBA Finals Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese came through for her team when it mattered most, leading them to victory over the Golden State Valkyries on Thursday to force a historic Game 7 in the WNBA Finals. Reese and her Dream teammates dealt with adversity after losing a 2-1 lead, and she detailed how the team responded and saved their season with the Game 6 victory. Angel Reese Says Dream Are Confident Heading Into Game 7 of WNBA Finals Reese revealed the key to the Dream’s strong bounce-back performance while speaking to the media after the game. “I think it started with us being able to have a little players-only meeting before film and talking through things, getting our confidence, getting our swagger back,” Reese said . “You can definitely tell that we got our swagger back.” A week ago, Reese seemed to be cruising towards being named Finals MVP before the Valkyries responded to win Games 4 and 5 of the series. Reese struggled in both games and received strong criticism from fans and analysts. However, she responded in Game 6, finishing the Dream’s 80-69 win over the Valkyries with 15 points, 14 rebounds, and 6 assists. MORE: ‘Historic,’ ‘No Caitlin Clark Fan Can Slander Her Again’ – WNBA World Hypes Up Angel Reese’s Performance As Dream Force Game 7 vs. Valkyries She cited the Dream’s ability to punch first, as Atlanta won the first quarter 32-15, essentially sealing the game after 10 minutes. The Valkyries struggled defensively, as multiple Dream players hit wide-open threes. Reese helped set the tone, but her All-Star teammates also had great performances. Guard Rhyne Howard, who might be Reese’s top competition for Finals MVP if the Dream win the championship, scored 21 points and has been the team’s most consistent scoring threat during the Finals. Reese was especially proud of guard Allisha Gray, who scored 23 points and returned to form after struggling on both ends of the floor in Games 4 and 5. Gray is playing through a hand injury but appears to have her confidence back heading into Game 7. The Dream clearly played with a sense of urgency at the start of Game 6, and they’ll look to do the same in Game 7 to win the WNBA championship. Reese and her teammates are aware that the Valkyries regained some momentum in the second half of Game 6 even though they lost. The Valkyries were down by 25 points but eventually cut the deficit to single digits as they made a second-half run. As the Finals head back to the Bay Area for the WNBA season’s final chapter, Reese and her teammates are confident their swagger is back and they can finish the job. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Barcelona close Camp Nou stand for Alavés clash after Eduardo Camavinga assault
item.description: Barcelona close Camp Nou stand for Alavés clash after Eduardo Camavinga assault La Liga giants Barcelona have made the call to close one of the home stands inside the Spotify Camp Nou for the club’s next La Liga outing. This comes owing to developments in last weekend’s showdown between the Blaugrana and arch rivals Real Madrid. After Kylian Mbappé netted an 88th-minute winner in Catalunya’s capital, chaos erupted in the ‘Gol 1957’ stand at the Camp Nou. Objects came raining down on top of Real Madrid’s players, whilst Eduardo Camavinga was struck by a fan with a Barcelona flag. The incident has since given rise to an official investigation, with the supporter responsible in line for a serious punishment. And as alluded to above, this week, those in a position of power at Barcelona have opted to take action of their own. As per a report from Goal , citing an official statement released by the reigning Spanish champions: ‘Barcelona have decided to suspend the activity of the Gol 1957 stand, known as the supporters’ stand, during the upcoming league match against Alavés. ‘This decision comes in response to a series of disciplinary proceedings opened against the club and some of its members, on the back of behaviour that runs contrary to sporting values. These actions expose the club to financial penalties, to the risk of the stadium being closed, as well as damaging its image. ‘The club will meet with representatives of the groups that make up the Gol 1957 stand to discuss the situation and determine the commitments necessary to maintain passionate and respectful support that contributes to backing the team without putting Barcelona’s property or reputation at risk. ‘The club’s wish is for the Gol 1957 stand to return to operating at full capacity during the Aston Villa match, provided that these discussions allow the situation to be rectified and ensure the proper running of things. ‘Support is an important element the club wishes to preserve, stemming from the shared commitment and responsibility of everyone, for the benefit of Barcelona.’ Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Packers’ Micah Parsons Reveals Attempt to Recruit Rival Coach Over Jonathan Gannon
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - SEPTEMBER 24: Micah Parsons #1 of the Green Bay Packers looks on prior to the start of the third quarter of the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field on September 24, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers have gotten strong results from Jonathan Gannon’s defense, even without Micah Parsons on the field. But their star pass rusher apparently had another coach in mind when the team searched for Jeff Hafley’s replacement earlier this year. Parsons has discussed trying to bring Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores to Green Bay, adding an interesting twist to a hiring process that eventually ended with Gannon getting the job. Micah Parsons Discusses Packers Recruiting Attempt for Brian Flores In a clip shared Thursday by Bleacher Report, Parsons discussed his attempt to recruit Flores, the defensive coordinator of Green Bay’s NFC North rival, while the Packers were looking for a new defensive leader. Parsons said that when the Packers were looking to hire their new defensive coordinator, he called Flores to see if he would be interested in coming to Green Bay. “I called him up and I’m like, ‘Hey B, you want to come up and coach me?'” Parsons said. “I’m trying to recruit him to Green Bay. He said, ‘Man, I love you and who you are, what you represent and how you play… But I gave these people my word I’m coming back to Minnesota.” The interest makes sense given how highly Parsons has spoken about Flores for years. Back when Parsons played for the Dallas Cowboys , he recalled meeting Flores during the pre-draft process and coming away impressed with the coach. “This dude is serious,” Parsons said in earlier comments about Flores, quoted in previous remarks about Flores . Green Bay had an opening in January after Hafley left to become head coach of the Miami Dolphins . Flores’ future in Minnesota was also being discussed around the league, although the Vikings announced a contract extension for him on Jan. 21. Four days later, reports emerged that the Packers were hiring Gannon, the former Arizona Cardinals head coach. Green Bay officially announced the move on Feb. 2. There is an important distinction between Parsons preferring to work with Flores during the search and wanting Gannon removed now. Parsons has also spoken positively about his current coordinator, and there is no indication that Green Bay is reconsidering the position. Packers’ Jonathan Gannon Has Earned Micah Parsons’ Support Parsons praised Gannon in May, after speaking with players who had previously worked under the new coordinator. “I’m extremely excited of what JG is going to bring to the team,” Parsons told The Action Network’s DJ Siddiqi . Gannon also met Parsons during his interview trip to Green Bay, when Parsons was at the team facility continuing his rehabilitation from a torn ACL. The Packers had already interviewed several candidates before choosing the former Eagles

item.title: Sting Ray Robb Is Trading Open-Wheel Solitude for 47-Car Traffic. That’s the Real Test.
item.description: Photo: City of Detroit / Wikimedia Commons (Public Domain) Sting Ray Robb’s move to United Autosports for the 2026/27 Asian Le Mans Series will be packaged as an IndyCar driver trying sports cars. That undersells it. The more useful read is that Robb has signed up for an exam in a skill IndyCar almost never tests: going fast through a crowd of slower cars, then handing a hot seat to two other drivers. The confirmed part is simple. United announced on October 28 that Robb, 25, will drive its No. 22 ORECA 07 LMP2 car alongside Ian Aguilera and Giorgio Roda. The season is six four-hour races across three European double-headers: Paul Ricard on November 13–15, Jerez on January 15–17 and Portimão on February 19–21. The series says it moved the whole calendar to Europe temporarily, away from the Middle East. The traffic is the exam Here is the number that matters. The series capped its full-season grid at 47 entries: two Ferrari 499P Hypercars, 16 LMP2 cars and 29 GT3 cars. Robb’s ORECA will spend most of every stint catching cars from a slower class, since GT3 machines are roughly six in ten of the field. That is my read of why this is harder than it looks. In a single-class series, every car ahead is a rival, and passing is a fight. In LMP2, most of the cars you catch are not rivals at all. The job is to get by cleanly without losing a second to the move or costing someone else their race. It is judgment more than outright speed, and it is the one thing a single-seater résumé can’t show. United Autosports’ No. 22 ORECA 07 at Watkins Glen in 2025, the same model and car number Robb will share in Europe. Photo: SmackJam / Wikimedia Commons ( CC BY-SA 4.0 ) A résumé that explains the appeal IndyCar’s own driver page lists Robb with 69 career starts and no wins or top-five finishes. He finished 2026 25th in points in the No. 77 Juncos Hollinger Chevrolet, in a season that ended with the finale at Laguna Seca . There are bright spots: United points to the 23 laps he led at the 2024 Indianapolis 500. So the attraction is easy to see. United is the 2026 European Le Mans Series champion, which makes this a car that is expected to win. Robb himself framed it that way, saying the goal is “to fight at the front and win races.” For a driver whose IndyCar results have rarely matched his seat time, a front-running ride is the rarest thing on offer. United’s announcement says nothing about his 2027 IndyCar plans, and this is not a comment on them. The teammates set the bar Robb is not walking into an empty car. Roda took five poles from six qualifying sessions with United last winter, according to the team, and Aguilera, 19, finished fifth in LMP2 on his Le Mans debut in 2026. In a three-driver crew the slowest stint is everyone’s problem, so Robb will be measured against a proven one-lap qualifier and a teenager with a Le Mans class result. United’s other entry, the No. 2, runs Phil Fayer, Hunter McElrea and Mikkel Jensen. McElrea is an IndyCar reserve driver and

item.title: Giants Emerge as Potential Trade Suitor for Future Hall of Famer
item.description: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 11: Head coach John Harbaugh of the New York Giants looks on during the fourth quarter of the game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) Getty The New York Giants, sitting alone atop the NFC East at 4-2-1, have been named as a potential trade suitor to watch for Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack. FanSided’s Michael Haney was the one who suggested Mack as a potential target to watch. With the Chargers remaining the NFL’s only winless team at 0-6, general manager Joe Schoen could find a low-cost opportunity to address a thinned-out edge room. The Giants have positioned themselves as buyers at the Nov. 10 trade deadline after a strong start under first-year head coach John Harbaugh. Their defense, coordinated by Dennard Wilson, has shown promise but carries clear vulnerabilities on the perimeter. Edge Room Needs Reinforcement Brian Burns, the team’s highest-paid defender, suffered a season-ending ACL tear early in the year, removing the unit’s most proven pass-rush presence. Kayvon Thibodeaux has logged a heavy snap share in Burns’ absence yet has recorded zero sacks through roughly six games while playing on a fifth-year option worth more than $14 million. Thibodeaux has contributed in the run game at times, but his pass-rush production has lagged, making him a possible trade candidate himself. Rookie Abdul Carter has stepped up with strong pressure rates and high marks from Pro Football Focus, yet the Giants remain limited when facing physical run schemes. Haney noted that without Burns, the edge group lacks the consistent edge-setting needed for Wilson’s aggressive scheme. Mack, a 13-year veteran, would represent an immediate upgrade over Thibodeaux in that specific area. Veteran Presence Could Stabilize Front Mack has recorded three sacks and 19 total tackles in six games this season for the Chargers while ranking among the league’s more reliable run defenders at the position. He entered 2026 with 116 career sacks and a long track record of setting the edge, a trait that distinguishes him from pure speed rushers such as Carter and Burns. Haney wrote that Mack is stronger against the run than either of those players and would strengthen the Giants’ ability to contain outside runs. The analysis suggests Schoen should pursue the deal if the cost is only a fourth-round pick, preserving future draft capital while adding a proven veteran. Mack is playing on a one-year contract, limiting long-term salary commitments for a contending Giants team. Adding him would allow the coaching staff to rotate Thibodeaux or move him if a favorable offer arrives. The Giants’ defensive front has been among the more productive units in the league when healthy, but depth has become a clear concern after Burns’ injury and other attrition. A short-term addition like Mack could help maintain momentum as New York aims for a division title

item.title: Anna Cockrell wants to cap emotional LA homecoming with greatest personal feat
item.description: Anna Cockrell already has an Olympic silver medal. Now she wants two golds, and she knows exactly where she wants to win them. She wants to stand on the top of the podium inside the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, where the former USC track and field superstar spent countless Saturdays cheering on the Trojans. Cockrell hopes to write the next chapter of her remarkable career when the Games return to Los Angeles in 2028. Olympic medalist Anna Cockrell poses during the The Nike After Dark Tour. DOMINIQUE POWERS In an exclusive interview with the California Post ahead of Nike’s sold-out After Dark Tour half- marathon in Redondo Beach last Saturday, the 29-year-old revealed that she’s targeting Olympic gold in the women’s 400-meter hurdles and the 4×400 meter relay at LA28. “Of course I want gold,” Cockrell said. “And on top of that, like, I want to be on the relay, too. So I got to get my flat 400 time down because I don’t want one, I want two. We’re trying to double up next time.” It’s an ambitious declaration from an athlete who has already conquered adversity, battled her own demons and climbed onto an Olympic podium. But perhaps the most intriguing part of Cockrell’s pursuit of gold isn’t the destination. It’s the road that brought her back to Los Angeles. Anna Cockrell of the USC Trojans celebrates after winning the women’s 400-meter hurdles at the NCAA track championships in Eugene, Ore., Saturday, June 12, 2021. NCAA Photos via Getty Images When Cockrell first arrived at USC from North Carolina a decade ago, she wasn’t exactly enamored with the City of Angels. “This is blasphemous to say now, but when I first arrived at USC, I didn’t love LA,” Cockrell admitted. “Because LA is just so big.” She had dreamed of leaving home and making a name for herself in a major city. Once she arrived, however, the reality was considerably more intimidating. Eventually, she found her footing, her friends and her family away from home. She also became one of the most decorated hurdlers in USC history, winning three individual NCAA championships, including a historic sweep of the 100-meter and 400-meter hurdles in 2021. But her college experience wasn’t all championships and celebrations. “As many wins as I had, there were big losses I had as well,” Cockrell said. “And I had a timeline in my mind of how my career would go, especially in college. And it took me longer than I expected.” Olympic medalist Anna Cockrell poses during the The Nike After Dark Tour. Those struggles helped shape the athlete who eventually won silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics, running a personal-best 51.87 seconds in the 400 hurdles behind American teammate Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone. Now, with the Olympics returning to Southern California, the possibility of competing inside the Coliseum feels almost too perfect. “I spent so many Saturdays at football games at the Coliseum,” Cockrell said. “So to be able to run in the Coliseum, for them to bring a track back, would be full circle.” The ir

item.title: Arsenal legend draws on his own teenage setback to back Max Dowman after Arsenal red-card appeal fails
item.description: Arsenal legend draws on his own teenage setback to back Max Dowman after Arsenal red-card appeal fails Ray Parlour has backed Max Dowman to bounce back from his first-team red card, drawing on his own experience of making a costly mistake as a teenager at Liverpool to urge the Arsenal youngster to learn from the setback. Arsenal’s appeal against Dowman’s dismissal in Tuesday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Fleetwood Town has been rejected, leaving the 16-year-old facing a three-match domestic suspension. Dowman was sent off late on for kicking out at Harrison Neal following a heavy challenge, compounding a frustrating evening for Mikel Arteta’s side, who were knocked out on penalties. But Arsenal Invincible Parlour believes the teenager can emerge stronger from the experience, having himself endured an uncomfortable introduction to senior football at Anfield. The former Arsenal midfielder was 18 when he made his debut against Liverpool in January 1992 — and marked the occasion by conceding a penalty. “I played alongside Dave Rocastle, the brilliant Dave Rocastle, in central midfield, and we were going really well,” Parlour told Hayters. “Then, 44th minute, I gave away a penalty for a foul on Ronnie Rosenthal. “I always remember Tony Adams going, ‘Ray, have you got the ball?’ I said, ‘No, Tony, I didn’t get the ball. I wish I did get the ball, Tony.’ “I thought George Graham would go mad at half-time. But he was good as gold. ‘Well done, son. Keep going.’” Parlour’s first appearance at one of English football’s most intimidating grounds could easily have become a painful memory. Instead, he used it as a learning experience, returning to Liverpool the following season withg a starring role in a winning side. “The following I went back, we won and I got man of the match,” he said. “So, again, that’s what you’ve got to do. It works.” It is a message he believes Dowman, who impressed against Everton at the weekend, must take into his own early career. The teenager has experienced the highs of making another appearance in Arsenal’s first team and the disappointment of a red card within days. “As I said, Max Dowman, he’d be on a high when he played well against Everton at the weekend, and then he’d be on a bit of a low when he got sent off the other night,” Parlour said. “But you’ve got to learn from your mistakes. You’ve got to learn certain bits. Football is a rollercoaster ride. You ain’t going to get ups all the time. You’re going to get a few downs. It’s how you respond to the downs, probably. “And I’m sure Max will be fine.” Parlour felt Dowman was unfortunate to be dismissed, questioning whether the incident might have been viewed differently had the player been older. “I thought he was unlucky, if I’m being honest,” he said. “But, you know, he’s been sent off. It’s still a red card. The ref could have seen it differently. I don’t think the red was needed. But it’s happened. So, you’ve just got to learn from that. “Mikel Arteta’s been there as a youngste

item.title: Diamondbacks star Corbin Burnes staying with Arizona after injury-plagued season
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Diamondbacks star Corbin Burnes staying with Arizona after injury-plagued season appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Arizona Diamondbacks right-hander Corbin Burnes will remain with the club after deciding against opting out of his contract , committing to four more seasons worth $140 million through 2030, USA Today’s Bob Nightengale reported on Thursday. The former National League Cy Young Award winner will collect $35 million annually from 2027 through 2030, although $11 million per season will be deferred. Burnes signed a six-year, $210 million contract with Arizona in December 2024, making it the largest deal in franchise history at the time, surpassing Zack Greinke’s $206.5 million agreement from 2015. However, injuries have considerably limited his contributions during the first two years of the partnership. The 2021 NL Cy Young Award winner made 11 starts in 2025 before undergoing Tommy John surgery in June after suffering a torn ulnar collateral ligament. His recovery extended into the following season, with a teres major strain in June delaying his anticipated return. Although Burnes eventually came off the injured list in September 2026, he managed only three starts before shoulder inflammation sidelined him again. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) His limited appearances yielded disappointing results. Burnes surrendered nine earned runs across 10.1 innings, recording a 7.84 ERA while allowing five home runs. His velocity and command were inconsistent, and he was unable to effectively utilize his cutter. In his final outing, he gave up three home runs in 2.2 innings. Nevertheless, the Diamondbacks remain hopeful that a full offseason will help Burnes recover his previous form. The shoulder inflammation is not expected to become a long-term issue, although his workload could be restricted after missing most of the past two seasons. Burnes own a career 3.20 ERA across 213 appearances, including a 2.86 ERA from 2020 through 2025. He will turn 32 before the 2027 season begins. His decision also leaves Arizona responsible for the remaining financial commitment, even as the organization is expected to reduce its payroll to some extent next season. Burnes reportedly turned down larger offers from other teams when signing with the Diamondbacks, with his family’s home in Scottsdale among the considerations behind that decision. With Burnes expected back in the rotation, Arizona can pair him with Eduardo Rodriguez, Merrill Kelly, Brandon Pfaadt and Ryne Nelson. Arizona could also explore bringing back Michael Soroka, who has a $10 million mutual option, or add another pitcher to bolster the starting staff. The Diamondbacks will now need their record-setting investment to prove its worth through consistent production, with Burnes’ health and effectiveness central to the rotation’s outlook for 2027 and beyond.

item.title: Omitted candidates: INEC upholds 41 of governorship petitions, rejects 28
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has upheld 41 of the 69 petitions filed against the final list of governorship candidates for the 2027 general election, while rejecting 28. Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC) of the commission, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday night. According to him, the petitions came from 12 political parties across 26 states. He said, “The complaints concerned the omission of certain political parties, the wrongful inclusion of candidates of political parties whose names were not contained in the membership registers submitted by their political parties, and instances of alleged multiple nominations.” Haruna said the commission examined the complaints against its records and the law. “Following a review of the complaints, relevant records and applicable legal provisions, the Commission found merit in some representations and approved the inclusion of affected candidates and their political parties, while complaints found to be without merit were declined. “In addition, some names that were wrongfully published in the final list were removed after verifying that their names were not on the register. “The Commission also approved the removal of candidates whose nominations were found to be inconsistent with the applicable legal requirements,” the statement said. Although INEC did not name any candidate or state, a source had earlier revealed that the commission’s meeting on Thursday to review complaints from parties and candidates left out of the lists had cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections, subject to the outcome of pending court cases. The source also said the petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, seeking a review of his exclusion from the list, did not succeed. “Yes, Pantami has been cleared,” the source said when asked about the PDP governorship candidate in Gombe State. “He did not succeed,” the source said when asked about Adebutu. On the State Houses of Assembly, the commission said the decisions affecting candidates sponsored by political parties “were informed by specific complaints received and determined in accordance with the law and the Commission’s established criteria.” For those elections, INEC received 61 petitions from 11 political parties across 11 states. Twenty-five succeeded, while 36 failed. The commission said the affected candidates, political parties and states “will be reflected in the updated list on the Commission’s website.” “Once again, the Commission assures the public of its commitment to transparency and the credibility of the electoral process,” the statement said. item.title: Everton beat Newcastle 3-1 to reach League Cup quarter-finals
item.description: Everton swept into the League Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 win against Newcastle on Thursday as they booked a clash against giant-killers Fleetwood. David Moyes’s side took the lead through James Garner’s first-half goal at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. Hayden Hackney doubled the lead with his first goal since his close-season move from Middlesbrough. Everton striker Thierno Barry netted in the second half and Dan Burn’s reply for Newcastle came far too late to stop the Toffees ending their three-match winless run. Chasing their first League Cup final appearance in 43 years, Everton will travel to fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in the week commencing December 14. The ‘Cod Army’ caused one of the biggest shocks in League Cup history on Tuesday when they beat Premier League champions Arsenal in a penalty shoot-out after a 1-1 draw at Highbury. Everton have never won the League Cup, losing their two final appearances in 1977 and 1984. Everton fans do not need reminding that it is 31 years since the club won the FA Cup in their most recent trophy triumph. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a noted Everton fan, is old enough to remember that success and he was cheering from the stands as Moyes’s men made light work of their last-16 tie. Newcastle will have the chance for revenge when the sides meet again in the Premier League at St James’ Park on Monday. Everton dropped a pre-match bombshell, saying Jack Grealish was unavailable for selection “due to a breach of club discipline”. Grealish, beset by criticism of his behaviour off the pitch, was reported to have taken an unauthorised absence from training. But the on-loan Manchester City winger’s absence was no problem for his team-mates. – Everton hit their stride – Newcastle tested Jordan Pickford early on when Joe Willock’s low drive was palmed away by the Everton goalkeeper, who repelled Fabian Schar’s long-range strike moments later. Garner steadied Everton’s nerves with a clinical opener in the 34th minute. Hackney teed up Garner just inside the area and the midfielder stretched to guide a fine finish into the far corner for his first goal since January. Everton had hit their stride and Hackney struck on the stroke of half-time. At the climax of a blistering Everton counter-attack, Barry hooked a cross into the six-yard box and Hackney timed his run perfectly to volley past Lukas Hornicek. Frustrated Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle sent on Joelinton, Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa at the interval. Wissa had an immediate chance after sprinting onto Willock’s pass, but he misjudged the high bounce and ended up heading straight at Pickford. It was a costly miss as Barry put the result beyond doubt in the 69th minute. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall provided the cross and Barry lashed home from close range for his seventh goal this season. item.title: 2027: Utomi, Ohaa, Yesufu urge Nigerians to mobilise support for Obi
item.description: Chieftains of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) have urged Nigerians to mobilise grassroots support for the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, come 2027. The party chieftains, including a political economist, Prof Pat Utomi, Enugu State NDC governorship candidate, Chief Chinyeaka Ohaa and human rights activist, Aisha Yesufu, made the call on Thursday during the Obi-Kwankwaso Town Hall Meeting held in Enugu. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Obi, his running mate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, and other NDC stakeholders attended the meeting, which attracted a large crowd of supporters. Addressing the crowd, Utomi expressed confidence that the Obi-Kwankwaso presidential ticket would provide the leadership needed to address Nigeria’s economic, political and security challenges. He lamented that Nigeria’s potential to become one of the greatest countries in the world had been undermined by corruption, criminality and disunity. According to him, the time has come for Nigerians to unite and work towards achieving meaningful political change. “We have done our research, and I know that a combination of Peter Gregory Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso will deliver Nigeria,” he said. Utomi urged Nigerians to turn out massively during the elections, vote for their preferred candidates and defend their votes through lawful means. In his remarks, Ohaa, the NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, described the Obi-Kwankwaso political alliance as a historic opportunity to strengthen national unity and promote inclusive governance. He said the partnership represented the possibility of building political bridges across Nigeria’s geopolitical zones. According to him, the alliance is reminiscent of the historic political understanding between the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe and Sir Ahmadu Bello during Nigeria’s early political development. “My message today is simple: we must seize this opportunity and work with our brothers and sisters across the South-South, South-West, North-East, North-West and North-Central to secure an NDC president in 2027,” he said. Ohaa explained that the campaign was not merely about producing a president of Igbo extraction but about establishing a government committed to justice, accountability, security and prosperity for all Nigerians. He expressed confidence that NDC candidates in Enugu State were prepared to earn the trust of voters and secure victory in the elections. Yesufu, a human rights activist, urged Nigerians to take ownership of the 2027 elections by mobilising voters and actively participating in the democratic process. She said the election was not merely about Obi’s presidential ambition but about the collective responsibility of Nigerians to rescue the country from its numerous challenges. item.description: In the future, you won’t be able to use Reddit without logging in. Reddit CEO Steve Huffman confirmed the impending change in a letter (PDF) to shareholders today about Q3 performance. He said that Reddit is shifting “to a logged-in-only experience," adding: Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them. It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally. It also allows us to protect access to Reddit’s extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world. item.title: Halloween Aboard the International Space Station
item.description: ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano finally gets his wish to fly like Superman aboard the International Space Station during Expedition 37. Although no ghouls, goblins, or trick-or-treaters come knocking at the International Space Station’s front hatch, crew members aboard the orbiting laboratory still like to get in the Halloween spirit. Whether individually or as an entire crew, they dress up in sometimes spooky, sometimes scary, but always creative costumes, often designed from materials available aboard the space station. Take a look at how the station crews have celebrated in years past. For Halloween 2009, the Expedition 21 crew shows off its costumes. Expedition 21 NASA astronaut Nicole Stott shows off her Halloween costume. In 2017, Expedition 53 crew members show off their Halloween costumes. Flight Engineer Sergei Prokopyev of Roscosmos, dressed as Elvis Presley, Commander Alexander Gerst of ESA as Darth Vader, and Flight Engineer Serena Auñón-Chancellor of NASA as a mad scientist, pose for a Halloween photo inside the Kibo Japanese Experiment Module pressurized module aboard the space station during Expedition 57. Members of Expedition 61, NASA astronaut Christina Koch, top left, ESA astronaut Luca Parmitano, and NASA astronauts Andrew “Drew” Morgan, and Jessica Meir, show off their Halloween spirit in 2019. Expedition 66 crewmembers NASA astronaut Shane Kimbrough, left, Thomas Pesquet of ESA, Akihiko Hoshide of JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency), and NASA astronaut Mark Vande Hei show off their Halloween cards. In 2022, Expedition 68 astronauts Koichi Wakata of JAXA, left, and NASA astronauts Francisco “Frank” Rubio, Nicole Mann, and Josh Cassada dressed as popular video game and cartoon characters, using stowage containers in their Halloween costumes and holding improvised trick-or-treat bags. Expedition 70 astronauts Jasmin Moghbeli of NASA, left, Satoshi Furukawa of JAXA, NASA astronaut Loral O’Hara, and ESA astronaut Andreas Mogensen celebrate Halloween 2023. A trio of Expedition 73 astronauts dressed for Halloween in 2025. Follow the astronauts aboard the space station to see how they celebrate holidays in space. The space station remains a vital scientific platform, providing the foundation needed to survive and thrive as humanity ventures into the unexplored territories of our universe.
